virginia-tech.about:
Virginia Tech's College of Engineering is one of the largest in the US, and its architecture, agriculture and business programmes are well regarded. The university also runs an Innovation Campus near Washington, D.C. focused on computing.

International applicants must report English test results by the materials deadline of their round. Students who completed four years in English-medium schools may be exempt.
virginia-tech.aid_intl: Limited for international students; Virginia Tech's general scholarship application (priority deadline 22 Jan) is used for university scholarships.
virginia-tech.tests: English: TOEFL iBT 80 (no subsection below 16) or 4.5 on the new scale (no subsection below 4.0), IELTS 6.5 (no sub-score below 6.5), Duolingo 115, PTE 59, Cambridge 176; SAT EBRW 550 or ACT English 24 also accepted.
requirements: Secondary school transcript (grades from the last 3-4 years)
English test: TOEFL 80 / 4.5, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115
Common App personal essay (up to 650 words)
Virginia Tech ungraded short-answer questions
Application fee (see Virginia Tech website); fee waivers available for eligible applicants
Proof of funds / certification of finances for the I-20 or study permit (after admission)
Valid passport (needed for the visa / study permit)

waseda-university.about:
Waseda, founded in 1882, is one of Japan's two leading private universities, with a large international student body and alumni across politics, business and media. Its English-based undergraduate options include the School of International Liberal Studies (SILS), the Global Studies in Japanese Cultures Program, and English tracks in political science and economics, social sciences and engineering.

Applicants submit documents online according to their school's guidelines, using whichever recognised exam results they hold. Waseda handles the Certificate of Eligibility for visa purposes for admitted students abroad, and some applicants receive reserved scholarships at the admission stage.
waseda-university.aid_intl: Pre-enrolment (reserved) scholarships are offered to some applicants at admission, plus special scholarship programmes listed by the International Admissions Office.
waseda-university.tests: Waseda accepts a wide range of standardized tests and school-leaving results: SAT, ACT, IB, A-level, Gaokao, GSAT, CSAT, HKDSE, AISSCE, Baccalauréat, Abitur and more. Required documents depend on the school and your education background.

yonsei-university.about:
Founded in 1885 by missionaries, Yonsei is one of Korea's oldest and most prestigious private universities, with its main Sinchon campus in Seoul and an International Campus in Songdo. It is strong in medicine (Severance Hospital), business, economics and engineering, and its Underwood International College (UIC) offers four-year English-taught liberal-arts degrees in fields such as economics, international studies, political science, life science and technology, and creative technology management.

International applicants to UIC apply online in a spring or fall round, submit school records, essays and recommendations, prove English proficiency, and are interviewed. Every international applicant is considered for admissions scholarships that can cover full tuition for four years.
yonsei-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships: all international UIC applicants are automatically considered for admissions scholarships up to full tuition for four years; further merit scholarships each semester.
yonsei-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement. UIC requires proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, CEFR certificate, IB English A, AP English or English-medium schooling) with no minimum score. Selection is by document review plus an interview. Korean-taught Yonsei programmes require TOPIK instead.
yonsei-university.gpa_note: Holistic document review (200 points) plus interview; strong academic records and English writing are expected.
requirements: High school transcripts
High school diploma (GED/home-school not accepted)
Application essays
Recommendation letter(s)
Proof of English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS/IB/AP or English-medium certificate; no minimum)
Interview
Passport and nationality documents of applicant and parents
Application fee

york-university.about:
York has campuses at Keele, Glendon (a bilingual English-French liberal-arts campus) and Markham, and is known for business, law and society, fine arts and media, and kinesiology. Toronto's job market and York's co-op and experiential-learning options are major draws.

International tuition for most programmes is around CAD 40,000 per year. The President's International Scholarship of Excellence is worth CAD 45,000 a year for four years for top international high-school applicants with strong leadership and service.
york-university.aid_intl: Entrance scholarships for international students, including the President's International Scholarship of Excellence (CAD 180,000 over 4 years) and programme awards such as the CAD 25,000 Yavin Family International Science Student Scholarship.
york-university.tests: SAT/ACT not required. English proficiency required for applicants whose first language is not English (see York international requirements).
requirements: Secondary school transcript (grades from the last 3-4 years)
Secondary school diploma / final exam results (predicted results accepted when applying)
OUAC 105 online application (international applicants to Ontario universities)
English test: required for non-native speakers
Supplementary application for some programmes (e.g. fine arts, business)
Application fee (see OUAC/York)
Proof of funds / certification of finances for the I-20 or study permit (after admission)
Valid passport (needed for the visa / study permit)

zhejiang-university.about:
Zhejiang University is a comprehensive research university with several campuses in Hangzhou (Zijingang is the largest) plus the ZJU International Campus in Haining, home to joint institutes with the University of Edinburgh and the University of Illinois. It is particularly known for engineering, computer science and AI, agriculture and medicine, and for close links with Hangzhou's tech industry.

International undergraduates apply online with school records, a study plan, language certificates and, from 2026/27, a CSCA report; shortlisted candidates are interviewed by video and must prepay first-year tuition to confirm a place. Chinese-taught programmes require HSK, while English-taught ones require TOEFL/IELTS.
zhejiang-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship and Zhejiang Government Scholarship (Chinese-taught programmes only); programme-specific scholarships for some English-taught programmes (ZJU-UoE Institute, Global Communication and Management, MBBS).
zhejiang-university.tests: SAT/ACT/IB/A-level or national exam results are submitted if applicable (not mandatory). From 2026/27 all international undergraduate applicants must submit a valid CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report. Chinese-taught programmes need an HSK certificate; English-taught programmes need TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent (no published minimum). Shortlisted applicants have a video interview.
zhejiang-university.gpa_note: Competitive selection on senior-high academic performance, language proficiency, CSCA results and interview.
requirements: Senior high school transcripts
High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Study plan / personal statement
TOEFL/IELTS for English-taught programmes; HSK for Chinese-taught
CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report
SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results if applicable
Video interview if shortlisted
Passport valid beyond 1 March 2027
Application fee (RMB 800)
